📺 Beef (2023–Present)

Beef follows Danny Cho, a struggling contractor, and Amy Lau, a successful entrepreneur, whose lives become dangerously connected after a heated road rage incident in Los Angeles. What begins as a brief confrontation between two strangers quickly develops into an escalating feud filled with revenge, deception, and increasingly outrageous decisions. As Danny and Amy become obsessed with getting even, their personal lives, relationships, and careers begin falling apart. Beneath their anger, both are dealing with hidden frustrations, family pressures, and emotional struggles that reveal how much they have in common. Starring Steven Yeun and Ali Wong, the series combines dark comedy, intense drama, and unexpected twists while exploring anger, identity, loneliness, family, and the destructive consequences of refusing to let go.

🎭 Genre: Comedy • Drama • Dark Comedy • Thriller

⭐ IMDb: 8.0/10

⏱️ Runtime: Approximately 30–40 minutes per episode • TV-MA

🎥 Creator: Lee Sung Jin

🏆 Awards: Winner of eight Primetime Emmy Awards, including Outstanding Limited or Anthology Series.

📺 Where to Watch: Netflix in the United States.

source_details.synopsis: Beef is an American comedy drama anthology television series created by Lee Sung Jin for Netflix. Season 1 stars Steven Yeun and Ali Wong as Danny Cho and Amy Lau, two strangers whose involvement in a road rage incident escalates into a prolonged feud. Appearing in supporting roles are Joseph Lee, Young Mazino, David Choe, and Patti Yasutake. Season 2 stars Oscar Isaac and Carey Mulligan as Joshua Martín and Lindsay Crane-Martín, and Cailee Spaeny and Charles Melton as Ashley and Austin, two couples; after the poor latter two blackmail the rich former two with footage of a heated argument that would threaten their image, a similarly prolonged feud ensues.
